newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo shares fall after analyst meeting.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo shares fall after analyst meeting.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc stock fell on Wednesday after the company disappointed analysts with its outlook on earnings and U.S. beverage sales, traders and analysts said.
Pepsi officials could not be immediately reached for comment, but traders said the company presented weaker-than-expected earnings growth projections during a meeting with analysts.
In late afternoon trading, Pepsi's shares were down 2-1/4 at 36 on volume of more than 6.5 million shares.

According to analyst Edward Froelich of the Pershing division of Donaldson Lufin & Jenrette, Pepsi said some of its projected 15 percent earnings growth for next year and beyond would come from the sale of assets, rather than solely from increased business.
"That means Pepsi's EPS is not all organic growth but will be boosted by asset sales," Froelich said.

Schroeder Wertheim analyst Caroline Levy cut her earnings estimates for Pepsi's second quarter on the outlook. She now estimates Pepsi's earnings will show little change from the second quarter of last year, when it earned $0.36 a share. Earlier she estimated Pepsi's 1997 second-quarter profit at $0.38.
Froelich said some of the assets that Pepsi might be considering selling include extraneous bottling divisions.

The company on Monday said it would restructure its bottling operations into a separate unit with its own management structure. At the time, analysts said the move a prelude to a spinoff of the bottling operations.
Pepsi, however, denied it was preparing for a spinoff.
